literal: O shining jeweled one! Today if I forget, my shoulders upon ornaments will slip off, beauty having shed.
translation: O wearer of shining jewels! If I try to forget him even for a single day, my shoulders will lose their beauty and the ornaments on them will slip off.
modern: விளங்கும் அணிகலன்களை அணிந்த தோழியே! இன்று ஒருநாள் நான் அவரை மறக்க நினைத்தால், என் தோள்கள் தம் அழகை இழந்து, அவற்றின் மேல் உள்ள வளையல்களும் அணிகலன்களும் கழன்று விழுந்துவிடும்.
explanation: In this couplet, the heroine speaks to her close friend who is adorned with bright jewels. She explains that she cannot afford to forget her beloved even for a single day to ease her pain. The moment she attempts to forget him, the grief of separation causes her body to waste away instantly. As her shoulders grow thin and lose their natural beauty (kārikai), the bracelets and ornaments (kalam) worn on them will lose their grip and slip off. This physical change serves as an immediate, visible sign of her deep yearning and the impossibility of forgetting him.
